introduction: “Some imagined for God, according to their own delusions, certain attributes … and form.” The guide gathers statements that God has no body, place or likeness; that even will, knowledge and power, as we mean them, are our way of speaking; that the “image” of Genesis is not a shape; and that the Manifestations are mirrors and not God made flesh. Then it reports, sharply, a disagreement with Christian doctrine. Xenophanes said it first among the Greeks, with his horses painting horse-gods; Isaiah, the Qur’an and the rabbis say it within the religions of the Book. The Bible also says that God repented, and John that the Word was made flesh; Paul speaks of the fulness of the Godhead dwelling bodily; and Nicaea reached for “Light of Light”. Those are placed here as the tradition speaking for itself, which the guide’s own arc asks for. Feuerbach marks the other edge: the thinker who concluded that all the attributes, and the God who bears them, are human.
questions: Xenophanes’ horses would paint gods like horses. If every image of God is drawn from ourselves, what do the readings say can still be truly said of God?
Scripture says both that God is not a man that he should repent and that the Lord repented. How does “the Torah speaks in the language of men” help, and does it explain too much?
Feuerbach agrees that the divine attributes are human ones. Where exactly do the readings part from him?
State the doctrine of the Incarnation as John and Paul state it. Now state reading 10. Is the difference between a mirror and an incarnation one of words, of emphasis, or of substance?

outside.why: Some imagined for God a form “according to their own delusions”. Xenophanes, five centuries before Christ: if oxen and horses had hands and could paint, horses would paint the forms of the gods like horses, and oxen like oxen.
To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?
The reading comments on this chapter of the Qur’an: Say: He is God, the One! God, the eternally Besought of all! He begetteth not nor was begotten. And there is none comparable unto Him.
“God changes not with the changes of creation.” God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent.

The same scriptures say, after the golden calf: and the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Bible speaks both ways. How does a reader who holds reading 4 take such verses?
God has no place, substance or limit. The Qur’an: naught is as His likeness; and He is the Hearer, the Seer.
The attributes we ascribe, will, knowledge, power, reflect what we see in creatures. The rabbis’ rule for every such expression in scripture: the Torah speaks in the language of men.

Feuerbach took the same observation to its end: the attributes we give God are human attributes set outside us, and theology is anthropology. The reading agrees about the attributes and keeps the Reality beyond them. What grounds that step, which he refused?
The reading quotes this verse, and says image and likeness do not refer to bodily form: let us make man in our image, after our likeness.
God “doth in no wise manifest His inmost Essence”. No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.

Bahá’ís “do not believe in the incarnation of the Word”. Christians confess exactly that: the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory. To them this is not a limiting of God but his nearness. What do the two sides each fear to lose?
The Messengers are mirrors in which the image of the Sun appears. Hebrews of the Son: the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person.

The reading describes Catholic belief from outside. From inside it is Paul’s sentence: in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. How would one state the Christian doctrine so that a Christian would recognise it, before disagreeing?

The cross and the Trinity are called anthropomorphism. The Nicene fathers, defining what they meant, chose the least bodily image they had: God of God, Light of Light. Is their formula an attempt to say what reading 11 says with its mirror, or something the readings must reject?
